[docs/resource-guides/ibm/queue.md#ibm-mq-queue-type-queue]
Send messages to (or read them from) a queue on an IBM MQ queue manager from a handler. **Not supported on IBM Cloud:** `queue` triggers. pskit can't make a Code Engine function run for each message. Options: For Kafka-style messaging, [Event Streams](topic.md) is usually simpler to reach from Python.

[docs/resource-guides/ibm/storage.md#ibm-cloud-object-storage-bucket-type-storage]
Read and write objects in a Cloud Object Storage (COS) bucket from a handler. **Not supported on IBM Cloud:** `storage` triggers (a function that runs when an object is uploaded). Watch the bucket from the [on-premises host](../../resources.md#storage-drivers) with `driver: ibm_cos` instead, or have the uploader call the function's URL.

[docs/resource-guides/ibm/topic.md#ibm-event-streams-topic-type-topic]
**Not supported on IBM Cloud:** `topic` triggers. pskit can't subscribe a Code Engine function to a topic. Consume it from the [on-premises host](../../resources.md#custom-drivers) with a `custom` Kafka driver class ([`examples/19-custom-drivers`](../../../examples/19-custom-drivers) has a Kafka template), or poll from an HTTP function that something calls.

[docs/resource-guides/onprem/cache.md#on-premises-caches-type-cache]
A Redis / Valkey (or Memcached) server your functions use as a cache. pskit never creates or watches it: declare it with `external: true`. To use Redis as a **queue** that triggers functions, see [queue.md](queue.md#redis--valkey) instead. One Redis server can serve both; give them separate keys or databases (`/0`, `/1`).

[docs/resource-guides/onprem/custom.md#other-on-premises-services-type-custom]
`custom` covers anything else functions talk to: an SMTP server, LDAP / Active Directory, an internal REST API, an Elasticsearch cluster, a file share. pskit only hands `connection` values to handlers (`external: true` is required). Not to be confused with the **custom driver** (`options.driver: custom`), which plugs your own class into a `queue` or `storage` resource so it can trigger functions: see [queue.md](queue.md#rabbitmq-or-kafka-nats--via-a-custom-driver).
